clue.text: Turn on "Best Ram In Show"?

parts.note: the star of a show is its best performer
a tup is a ram, the male sheep

explanation.surface: A rosette for the champion ram at an agricultural show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best Ram In Show' reads as a prize category at a country fair; the leftover words 'In Show' complete that picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To start up a machine is to switch it on, so the phrasal verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Instrument — one adopted by famous performer

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so the word for one goes inside the performer

parts.note: a star is a famous performer
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes up a new musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' puts I inside STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument, an example of the class.

clue.text: State from which Mahler's wife received a degree

indicators.note: receiving takes something in, so the degree goes inside the wife's name

parts.note: Alma Mahler was the wife of the composer Gustav Mahler
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: Mahler's widow picks up an honorary degree from an American state university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received' signals the container; 'State' is a US state, not a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the states of the USA, an example of the class.

clue.text: One who draws rank?

definitions.meaning: a team that draws a match ties it, so it is one that ties
a row or rank, as in seating

explanation.walkthrough: 'draws' suggests an artist, but it is the sporting sense: a game that ends level is tied.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level in a series, so it means a rank; one who ties a game is one who draws.

clue.text: Complexion of papers about novelist, revolutionary and vegetable, in reverse order

indicators.note: the pieces are listed in the clue from last to first, so they are assembled in the opposite order

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary
George Sand was a French novelist
C, for circa, means about
a ream is a quantity of paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a writer, a rebel and a vegetable, told back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists papers, about, novelist, revolutionary and vegetable; 'in reverse order' says to put them down from vegetable back to papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A peaches-and-cream complexion is a fair, rosy skin, so the idiom describes a complexion.

clue.text: Scarf provides partial soundproofing

definitions.meaning: a warm scarf worn round the neck
a silencer on an exhaust deadens noise, cutting sound without removing it

explanation.surface: A neck scarf keeps out some of the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffler is both a thick neck scarf and a device that deadens sound, as on a car exhaust.

clue.text: Second man and his loopy, eccentric ethics

parts.note: mo is a moment, a short time, a second
Ralph is a man's name

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Another man and his crazy, odd moral code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loopy' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'eccentric' rearranges HISLOOPY into ILOSOPHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral philosophy is the branch of study concerned with right and wrong, another name for ethics.

clue.text: Circle of politically correct gurus supplying advice to politician?

definitions.text: Circle of politically correct gurus supplying advice to politician?

parts.words: Circle of politically correct gurus supplying advice to politician
parts.note: a small hand-picked circle whose opinions are canvassed so that a politician can tune policy to what is acceptable

explanation.definitionFit: A focus group is a small sample of people whose views are canvassed to guide policy or marketing.

clue.text: Remarkably alert in site of evacuation

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something done in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stay alert where people are being evacuated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuation' suggests clearing people from danger; here it is of the bowels. 'Remarkably' rearranges ALERTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a toilet, the place where one empties the bowels, so it is a site of evacuation.

clue.text: Due consideration of muscle in repose

indicators.note: one word placed in another, the muscle within the rest

parts.note: repose means rest
pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: Proper regard for a muscle when it is relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; the muscle is a chest muscle, in its gym-slang short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect means proper regard or deference, the consideration that is due to someone.

clue.text: What Desmond Tutu would make of a commercial gathering?

definitions.text: What Desmond Tutu would make of a commercial gathering?

parts.words: What Desmond Tutu would make of a commercial gathering
parts.note: the archbishop, a campaigner for justice, would judge an equitable exchange of goods to be just, reading a business expo as an ethical verdict

explanation.walkthrough: The two words of the phrase can be read separately as a verdict that business is just, the sort a campaigner for justice like Archbishop Tutu would hope to give.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade fair is an exhibition where businesses show goods, a commercial gathering.

clue.text: Skin is censored in advance

indicators.note: in advance means placed before, so the censored word comes first

parts.note: a censored film has been cut

explanation.surface: Bare skin is snipped out before the film is shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in advance' says the censored word comes first, though the clue prints 'is' before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical term for the skin, the dermis and epidermis together.

clue.text: Hiding place turned over for money

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lair is an animal's hiding place

explanation.surface: A secret stash is overturned in search of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses LAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The rial is the currency of Iran and several other countries, an example of money.

clue.text: Unsophisticated popular song about "The Flower in the Wood"

indicators.note: the song and flower sit inside the tree's name

parts.note: pine is a wood

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the song wraps round the flower

parts.note: a hit is a popular song
lis is the lily, as in fleur-de-lis

explanation.surface: A lowbrow chart hit about a flower in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'in' signal the two containers. 'Flower' is not a river here but the heraldic lily of the fleur-de-lis.
explanation.definitionFit: A philistine is a person hostile to culture, so as an adjective it means uncultured or unsophisticated.

clue.text: What is the right translation of "rednecks"?

indicators.note: a translation renders words in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to render the term 'rednecks' in another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' rearranges WHATISTHE plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: White trash is a derogatory American term for poor white people, roughly what rednecks means too.

clue.text: Tubs in which love's an anticlimax

indicators.note: the tubs are a container, with love placed inside them

parts.note: baths are tubs
love is zero in tennis, hence O

explanation.surface: Romance in the bathtub turns out to be a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' puts O inside BATHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is a sudden lurch from the lofty to the trivial, a literary letdown or anticlimax.

clue.text: Bring in largely unyielding undergarment

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: hard means unyielding
a vest is an undergarment, in Britain worn under a shirt

explanation.surface: Bringing in an inflexible piece of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts HARD to HAR. In British English a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To harvest crops is to gather them in, so the verb is a synonym of bring in.

clue.text: Brown saint? Brown saint

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A holy man with a sun tan, mentioned twice for emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue repeats itself: the first 'Brown saint' builds DUN + S + TAN and the last 'saint' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: St Dunstan was a tenth-century Archbishop of Canterbury, an example of a saint.

clue.text: Display of animal behaviour by Cockney swine aboard boat

indicators.note: aboard means on the boat, so the swine are put inside it

parts.note: a dhow is an Arab sailing boat

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of a word

parts.note: hogs are swine

explanation.surface: Pigs on a ship behaving like animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney' drops the opening H, as the working-class London accent does; 'aboard' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog show displays animals for judging, with their bearing and obedience on show.

clue.text: Lady 9, taking drug but not drinking

parts.note: 9 is the number nine
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
E is ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A woman from Number 9 who takes drugs but stays off the booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninette is a woman's first name, so it names a lady.

clue.text: Meal involving a sending-off

indicators.note: involving means including, so the meal takes in the letter

parts.note: lunch is a meal

explanation.surface: A lunch at which a player is sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts A inside LUNCH. 'sending-off' looks like football but means dispatch.
explanation.definitionFit: The launch of a ship or rocket is its sending off on its way.

clue.text: Court officer's trap catches nothing

indicators.note: catches means captures, so the trap holds the nothing inside

parts.note: to corner someone is to trap them
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A court official's snare comes up empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' puts O inside CORNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner presides over a coroner's court investigating sudden deaths, so is an officer of a court.

clue.text: Scientist's nervous reaction is interrupting French playwright

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so these letters go inside the playwright

parts.note: Jean Genet was a French playwright
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A researcher's twitch breaks into a French dramatist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' puts TICIS inside GENET.
explanation.definitionFit: A geneticist studies heredity and genes, an example of a scientist.

clue.text: Second-rate low-lifer's objectionable offspring

parts.note: B is second grade, second-rate
a rat is a contemptible person, a low-lifer

explanation.surface: A lowlife's unpleasant child is second-rate too.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is a badly behaved child, so it is an objectionable offspring.

clue.text: Saint of the Riviera failing to finish figure of speech

indicators.note: failing to finish means the last letter is lost

parts.note: St Tropez is the Riviera resort named after Saint Tropez

explanation.surface: A Riviera saint cannot complete a rhetorical flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to finish' drops the Z of TROPEZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figurative use of a word, such as a metaphor, so it is a figure of speech.

clue.text: The cry of one bird or another

definitions.meaning: a second bird, the black corvid

explanation.walkthrough: 'one bird' is the cockerel, whose call this is; 'another' is a different bird of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow is a cock's call and also a black bird of the genus Corvus.

clue.text: Humble dwelling — one with a rodent

parts.note: a hut is a humble dwelling
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A modest cabin shared with a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: The hutia is a large Caribbean rodent, an example of the class.

clue.text: Unearthly power given to Muse to take name of language

parts.note: ESP, extra-sensory perception, is a paranormal power

indicators.note: take means take in, so the Muse holds the name inside

parts.note: Erato is the Muse of lyric poetry

explanation.surface: A supernatural gift and a Muse combine to name a tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' puts N inside ERATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international language devised by Zamenhof.

clue.text: Sound of impact when king enters town

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so the king goes inside the sound

parts.note: wham is the sound of a heavy blow
rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A crash is heard as the monarch arrives in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' signals the container; the town is in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrexham is a town in north-east Wales, an example of the class.

clue.text: Common occupant of churchyard recorded address to trio in Ireland

indicators.note: recorded means heard as spoken, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: calling to three people, 'you three', in an Irish accent where 'three' is said as 'tree'

explanation.surface: Something common in a churchyard records a greeting to three Irish people.
explanation.walkthrough: Irish speech often says the 'th' in 'three' as a plain T, so 'you three' comes out as the tree's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Yews are long-lived evergreens traditionally planted in English churchyards, so one is a usual occupant.
